question: The intestinal absorption of iron is more effective:

options.opa: In the form of ferric ion.
options.opb: In the form of heme group.
options.opd: If there are oxalates in digestive light.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Iron in the form of heme group" -> "more effectively absorbed in the intestines" -> 80% CHAIN: "Iron in the form of ferric ion" -> "requires conversion to ferrous ion for absorption" -> "less effective absorption compared to heme iron" -> 70% CHAIN: "Iron absorbed via the transferrin membrane transporter" -> "facilitates efficient uptake of iron into cells" -> 85% CHAIN: "Presence of oxalates in the digestive tract" -> "can bind to iron and inhibit absorption" -> "reduced effectiveness of iron absorption" -> 80%
enhanced_information: Iron in the form of heme group is more effectively absorbed in the intestines compared to ferric ion. Absorption via the transferrin membrane transporter facilitates efficient uptake of iron into cells. The presence of oxalates in the digestive tract can bind to iron and inhibit absorption, reducing its effectiveness.
analysis: The most effective form of iron absorption in the intestine is via the heme group, which is found in animal-based foods. Heme iron is more readily absorbed compared to non-heme iron forms like ferric ion. Transferrin membrane transporter is involved in iron transport within the body but not in direct absorption from the intestine. Oxalates in the digestive tract can actually inhibit iron absorption.
